caption:
Global Metadata
Basic Attributes: bpm is 70. key is G major, and scale is major. Cinematic Country-Pop Ballad, a father's proud, tender song about a small child who sees the world big.
Global Emotional Progression: The track opens on a single acoustic guitar with a restrained steel-guitar swell, the male lead gentle and proud, describing a child drawing a house with seven windows. The first verse adds a soft kick and a light, country-leaning brush rhythm. The chorus is the emotional peak of the verses: a full strum, a warm steel-guitar line and a low male harmony on the title phrase. The second verse is lighter, plucked banjo-like guitar and a soft bass, the child's animal kingdom made playful. The third verse is more tender, guitar and a soft string pad, the father's voice closer to the microphone as he describes her falls and her courage. The bridge is the song's turn, a full string section and a slower tempo feel with piano under the voice, the father promising to help her understand. The final chorus returns with every layer, a bright fiddle-like line and a wordless choir. The outro is guitar and voice alone, the title phrase repeated softly to the end.
Application Scenarios & Imagery: A child at a kitchen table drawing a house with seven windows, a rainbow pencilled over a sun, a row of plush animals lined up across a hallway, a playground where a small girl falls and stands up again, a father kneeling to tie a small pair of shoes, a family porch at dusk.
Sonics & Production Profile: Close, warm, small-room soundstage with the vocal forward and almost unprocessed. Natural acoustic polish: woody low end from upright bass and piano rather than synthetic sub-bass, generous midrange left intact, soft unhyped top end. Dynamics stay low and conversational in the verses and open gently rather than loudly in the choruses. Light room reverb on the instruments, with the lead vocal kept close and dry so every breath and consonant reads.

Vocal Details
Vocal Gender & Timbre: Singer A (Male). A warm, lived-in baritone in his late thirties, unhurried and close to the microphone in the low register, opening into a grainier and slightly frayed tone as he lifts into his upper chest voice.
Vocal Style: Confiding and nearly spoken in the verses, sitting right on the microphone with audible breath and soft consonants, as though the song is being said to one person rather than performed. The pre-chorus tightens the phrasing and lifts in pitch. The chorus is open-throated and plain, carried on feeling rather than power, with the catch left in the voice instead of smoothed away. The bridge falls back almost to speech before the final build.
Harmony/Backing Vocals: A single low male harmony a third beneath the lead thickens each chorus. A soft wordless pad of female and child-register voices joins the final chorus for warmth and height. Airy unison doubles of the lead drift beneath the outro.
Vocal FX: Close and dry lead with a short plate reverb and no audible delay through the verses. A gentle slapback opens on the choruses. The outro vocal is washed in a long soft reverb tail that decays into the room sound.

Arrangement
Instrument Lifecycle Description (Primary/Secondary Layering):
Primary: An acoustic guitar with a restrained steel-guitar line carries the whole song, and a warm upright bass holds the bottom. Secondary: A soft kick and a light brush rhythm enter with the chorus; banjo-like plucks colour the second verse; a string pad and a piano bed hold the third verse and the bridge; a fiddle-style line lifts the final chorus. Groove & Foundation Progression: A slow, country-leaning brush pulse with a steady backbeat in the chorus. The bridge drops to strings and piano with no drums, and the final chorus returns the full band. Embellishments, Textures & Spatial FX: A pencil scratching on paper under the first line, a child's laugh sampled faintly in the second verse, a warm room reverb on the steel guitar, and the outro's final soft guitar decay.
lyrics:
[intro]
You hold a pencil like a captain
Gripping hard the wheel,
You draw a house with seven windows
And a garden of a field.

[verse]
You say, this one is for Daddy,
This one's where the flowers grow,
Then you add a little rainbow
To a sky I used to know.
You solve your tiny puzzles
With a focus fierce and bright,
You turn the pieces over
Till the picture comes to light.
You may be small enough to fit
Inside my waiting arms,
But there is something powerful
In all your little charms.

[chorus]
Small hands, big world,
Big dreams in a little girl.
You carry more light
Than the stars in the night.
You teach my heart to see
Who I was and who I can be.
Small hands, big world,
You are my precious girl.
You make me laugh,
You make me strong,
You show me where my heart belongs.
And every day I understand
A better life begins
With your small hands in my hands.

[verse]
You lined your animals up
Across the hallway floor,
The lion was the teacher,
The rabbit guarded the door.
The little bear was sleeping,
The elephant was late,
And you explained the whole plan to me
With a serious little face.
You organise the whole world
In your wonderfully bright way,
You make a home from anything,
A game from any day.
Your mind is full of questions,
Your spirit full of flight,
You find a hundred possibilities
Inside a single night.

[verse]
Sometimes you fall and scrape your knee
And tears begin to rise,
You look at me, then stand again
With courage in your eyes.
I kiss the place that hurts you,
But you're stronger than the pain,
You take a breath and run again
Into the sun and rain.
I wish I could protect you
From every difficult road,
Carry every burden
And lighten every load.
But life will have its lessons,
And you'll learn them as you grow,
I'll be beside you, cheering
Every step you choose to go.

[pre-chorus]
You don't know it, little darling,
But you rescue me each day,
You bring my tired heart back home
In your own special way.

[chorus]
Small hands, big world,
Big dreams in a little girl.
You carry more light
Than the stars in the night.
You teach my heart to see
Who I was and who I can be.
Small hands, big world,
You are my precious girl.
You make me laugh,
You make me strong,
You show me where my heart belongs.
And every day I understand
A better life begins
With your small hands in my hands.

[bridge]
If the world tells you you're too small,
Remember what I know,
The strongest rivers start as drops,
The tallest trees once grew low.
A seed can split the earth apart,
A spark can light the sky,
And you have more inside your heart
Than you can see tonight.
So dream as wide as oceans,
Walk as far as you can see,
Be gentle with the world, my child,
But never hide your wings.
And if you ever lose your way,
I'll help you understand,
You'll always have your father's voice
And a place within his hands.

[chorus]
Small hands, big world,
Brave heart in a little girl.
You carry more hope
Than the wildest wind can blow.
You teach my heart to see
The best that life can be.
Small hands, big world,
You are my precious girl.
You make me laugh,
You make me strong,
You are the reason I belong.
And every day I understand
A better life begins
With your small hands in my hands.

[outro]
Small hands, big world,
My forever little girl.
No matter where you stand,
You'll always hold my hand.
